**Table and figure.** As above, grouped by level-IV ecoregion (`'us_l4name'`). X axis: % of that ecoregion's pixels with a significant *intended* (`r int_word`) effect. Y axis: ecoregion, ordered by that percentage. Single grey fill, no facets. Range across the `r nrow(res_eco$summary)` ecoregions: `r sprintf('%.2f', min(res_eco$summary$pct_sig))`% to `r sprintf('%.2f', max(res_eco$summary$pct_sig))`%.


#### Significant DART effects, through time

The same effects along the time axis and against the covariates that interact with it: how often a
significant effect occurred in each year since treatment, how large those effects were and when they
peaked, and how the per-polygon peak years distribute across treatments and ecoregions. Read the two
halves as separate questions - a year can carry a high significance rate with small effects, or the
reverse.

##### How does time since treatment affect significance?

This section attempts to answer two questions:

(1) How *often* does a significant effect show up in a given year? The stacked-direction figure immediately below.

(2) How *large* are those effects? The mean-effect table and figure further down. A year can have a handful of significant pixels that each moved a long way, or many pixels that each moved a little, and those are different results.

No weighting is used anywhere in this section. The mean effect per year is a plain arithmetic mean of `effect` over the significant pixels in that year, split by direction of effect, so the reported peak is the year whose significant pixels actually moved furthest rather than a significance-weighted compromise across the whole time series. Some weighting methods were checked and did not improve the results - see `weight_testing_summary.Rmd` for that analysis.

Everything in this section is drawn on the **truncated** series: `r if (is.na(year_trunc$trunc_at)) paste0('for this objective no year fell below the ', min_year_n_i, '-', year_trunc$metric, '-pixel threshold, so the full record to year ', year_trunc$last_kept, ' is used') else paste0('for this objective the record is cut at year ', year_trunc$last_kept, ', because year ', year_trunc$trunc_at, ' was the first with fewer than ', min_year_n_i, ' ', year_trunc$metric, ' pixels')`. This is what stops a peak year being reported from the part of the record where almost nothing was significant; it also means the x axis here can end earlier than another objective's, so the two are not read off the same range.

```{r results-5_17, echo = F}
sig_by_year <- s_0$input |>
  dplyr::group_by(year_diff) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_pix       = dplyr::n(),
    pct_sig     = round(100 * mean(sig), 2),
    pct_sig_pos = round(100 * mean(sig & effect > 0), 2),
    pct_sig_neg = round(100 * mean(sig & effect < 0), 2),
    .groups = 'drop'
  ) |>
  dplyr::arrange(year_diff)

# Sample-size labels are rotated upright (see plot_sig_direction_stacked()): the
# group total sits above each bar, and each stacked segment carries its own n -
# the count of pixels that were significant and positive, and significant and
# negative, respectively. `reverse_stack` is set from the objective so that the
# INTENDED direction is always the segment drawn against the x-axis, whichever
# direction that is for this objective.
plot_sig_direction_stacked(
  s_0$input, group_col = 'year_diff', reverse_stack = (int_word == 'positive'),
  x_lab = 'Years since treatment', x_break_by = 5,
  title = 'Significant DART effects through time, by direction',
  subtitle = paste0(print_summary_name(summaries, r_ind, 5), ' (', int_word, ' = intended)')
)

# Most and least effective year, pulled out of `sig_by_year` here so that the
# sentences below can be written as prose with inline R rather than printed as
# console output.
year_most  <- sig_by_year$year_diff[which.max(sig_by_year$pct_sig)]
year_least <- sig_by_year$year_diff[which.min(sig_by_year$pct_sig)]
pct_most   <- max(sig_by_year$pct_sig)
pct_least  <- min(sig_by_year$pct_sig)
```

**Figure.** X axis: years since treatment, one bar per year, labelled every 5 years. Y axis: the percentage of that year's pixels with a significant DART effect - the full height of a bar is the year's overall % significant, and it is a percentage of all pixels observed in that year, not of the significant ones. Fill: the direction of the significant effect, splitting each bar into a blue *significant negative* component and a red *significant positive* component; the intended direction for this objective (`r int_word`) is the segment drawn against the axis, with the unintended direction stacked above it. Fill colours mean the same thing in every direction figure in this report. There are no facets or other groupings.

Two different sample sizes are labelled on each bar, and they are **not** meant to sum to each other:

- The rotated label sitting *above* each bar is that year's **group total** - every pixel observed in that year, significant or not. It says how much data is behind the bar, and it is the denominator of the percentage on the Y axis.
- The white label *inside* each stacked segment is the number of pixels that were significant **and** in that segment's direction. These two are the sample sizes behind the two segment heights themselves.

So the two segment labels add up to the number of *significant* pixels in that year, which is generally far smaller than the group total above the bar, because most pixels in a year are not significant. Reading down a tall bar with a small group total is therefore a different situation from a short bar with a large one, which is exactly why both numbers are drawn. Segments too short to hold their label legibly are left unlabelled to avoid white text spilling onto the panel background.

- Treatment was **most** effective (highest % significant pixels) at year `r year_most` (`r sprintf('%.1f', pct_most)`% significant).
- Treatment was **least** effective (lowest % significant pixels) at year `r year_least` (`r sprintf('%.1f', pct_least)`% significant).

##### How large were the significant effects in each year?

The figure below switches from counting significant pixels to measuring them: among significant pixels only, what was the mean DART effect in each year since treatment, and in which year was that mean largest? Positive and negative effects are summarized separately throughout.

```{r results-5_18, echo = F}
# Both computed in 2_results_setup.R, which also keeps the copy that
# collect_obj_tables('peak_effect_') gathers for the compiled table in
# 2_make_DART_results.Rmd. The figure below is handed the peak table rather than
# recomputing it, so the dashed peak lines cannot disagree with the table above.
effect_by_year <- .st$effect_by_year
peak_effect    <- .st$peak_effect

knitr::kable(
  peak_effect,
  col.names = c('Direction', 'Peak Year', 'Mean Effect at Peak', 'SE', 'Significant Pixels at Peak', 'Last Year Observed', 'Peak Censored?'),
  digits = 4
)

# The peak table is handed to the figure rather than recomputed inside it, so the
# dashed peak-year lines and their labels can never disagree with the table above.
plot_mean_effect_year(
  effect_by_year,
  subtitle    = paste0(print_summary_name(summaries, r_ind, 5), ' (', int_word, ' = intended)'),
  peak_effect = peak_effect
)

# Written out as a character vector and emitted below with inline R, so the peak
# sentences appear as prose rather than as console output.
peak_bullets <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(peak_effect)), function(i) {
  pk <- peak_effect[i, ]
  sprintf(
    '- Significant **%s** effects were largest at year %s (mean effect %.4f, SE %.4f, n = %d significant pixels)%s.',
    pk$direction, pk$peak_year, pk$peak_effect, pk$peak_se, pk$peak_n_pix,
    ifelse(pk$is_censored, ', which is the last year observed for that direction - the effect may still have been growing past the end of the record', '')
  )
}, character(1))
```

**Table.** One row per direction of effect: the year in which the mean effect over significant pixels was largest in magnitude, that mean, its SE, the number of significant pixels behind it, the last year observed for that direction, and whether the peak is censored (lands on that last year).

**Figure.** X axis: years since treatment. Y axis: the mean DART effect (Δ RAP cover) among *significant pixels only* in that year, computed separately for each direction - so the two series sit either side of the zero line by construction and are never averaged into a single number. Colour: direction of the effect (red = significant positive, blue = significant negative), using the same colours as the stacked figure above. The shaded band around each line is that year × direction mean ± 1 SE: it is sampling uncertainty in the *mean* effect, not the spread of individual pixel effects, so it narrows mainly where a year has many significant pixels. A year × direction cell backed by a single significant pixel has no SE and is drawn as a bare point, keeping the line through it unbroken. Dashed vertical lines mark each direction's peak year from the table above, labelled with the mean effect at the peak, its SE, and the number of significant pixels behind it. Non-significant pixels are excluded outright rather than entered as zeros, and no weighting is applied anywhere. There are no facets or other groupings.

`r paste(peak_bullets, collapse = '\n')`

Note that the year with the largest mean effect need not be the year with the most significant pixels: the two questions can peak at different times, and a peak that lands on the last observed year is flagged as censored above for the same reason as in the by-polygon table further down.

```{r results-5_19, echo = F}
# The 1-5 / 6-10 / 11-15 / 16+ binning is done in 2_results_setup.R, on a local
# copy of the input so the frame in `summaries_mod` never picks up a
# reporting-only column.
sig_by_bin <- .st$sig_by_bin

knitr::kable(
  sig_by_bin,
  col.names = c('Objective', 'Cover', 'Year Bin', 'Total Pixels', 'Mean % Significant', 'Mean % Significant Positive', 'Mean % Significant Negative')
)
```

**Table.** The same significance rates as the year-by-year figure, collapsed into 1-5, 6-10, 11-15 and 16+ years since treatment. One row per bin; percentages are of all pixels in that bin, and the two directional columns sum to the overall column up to rounding.

```{r results-5_20, echo = F}
# --- By-polygon: which year_diff was each polygon's most/least significant, and
# is that peak/trough censored (i.e. does it land on the LAST year observed for
# that polygon, meaning we can't tell if it would have kept climbing/falling)?
# This is a hard per-polygon peak/trough year - the single year with the highest
# (or lowest) % significant pixels for that polygon, unweighted and unsmoothed.
# ---
poly_year_sig <- s_0$input |>
  dplyr::group_by(polygon, tx_coarse, us_l4name, year_diff) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_pix   = dplyr::n(),
    pct_sig = 100 * mean(sig),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )
poly_best_worst <- poly_year_sig |>
  dplyr::group_by(polygon, tx_coarse, us_l4name) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_years         = dplyr::n(),
    year_max        = year_diff[which.max(pct_sig)],
    year_min        = year_diff[which.min(pct_sig)],
    is_censored_max = year_max == max(year_diff),
    is_censored_min = year_min == max(year_diff),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

# Summarize each polygon's "peak significance year" across treatments and ecoregions
time_summary_by_tx <- poly_best_worst |>
  dplyr::group_by(tx_coarse) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_polygons        = dplyr::n(),
    mean_year_max     = round(mean(year_max), 2),
    sd_year_max       = round(sd(year_max), 2),
    min_year_max      = min(year_max),
    max_year_max      = max(year_max),
    pct_censored_max  = round(100 * mean(is_censored_max), 1),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

time_summary_by_eco <- poly_best_worst |>
  dplyr::group_by(us_l4name) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    n_polygons        = dplyr::n(),
    mean_year_max     = round(mean(year_max), 2),
    sd_year_max       = round(sd(year_max), 2),
    min_year_max      = min(year_max),
    max_year_max      = max(year_max),
    pct_censored_max  = round(100 * mean(is_censored_max), 1),
    .groups = 'drop'
  )

col_lab_time <- c('Group', 'N Polygons', 'Mean Year of Peak Sig.', 'SD', 'Min', 'Max', '% Censored (peak at last obs. year)')

# The SD of the peak year is undefined (NA) for any treatment or ecoregion backed
# by a single polygon - there is nothing to vary. Those cells are rendered blank
# rather than as a literal "NA", which reads as missing data rather than as a
# quantity that cannot exist. The option is set around these two calls only and
# restored afterwards, since kable() substitutes at call time.
old_na <- options(knitr.kable.NA = '')
knitr::kable(time_summary_by_tx,  col.names = c('Treatment', col_lab_time[-1]))
knitr::kable(time_summary_by_eco, col.names = c('Ecoregion', col_lab_time[-1]))
options(old_na)
```

**Tables.** Each polygon is reduced to the single year in which its own % significant pixels was highest ("peak significance year"); those per-polygon peak years are then summarized across polygons, by treatment in the first table and by ecoregion in the second. Columns: number of polygons behind the row, mean / SD / min / max of the peak year, and the percentage of polygons whose peak fell on the last year they were observed. A polygon's peak year is flagged as "censored" in those cases, because we can't rule out that significance was still rising beyond the end of the available time series. Note that "last year observed" now means the last year *retained* after the late-year truncation described above, so where a series was truncated the censoring flag is partly an artefact of the threshold rather than of the record itself - it marks the end of the analysable series, not necessarily the end of the data. What that censoring implies is taken up under *Interpretation* at the end of the report.

#### Overall results and interpretation

##### Summary statistics

What the three sample-size filters cost this objective x cover response, in one row - the same
quantities reported in prose under *Results after all three filters* above, gathered here so that this
subsection stands on its own. The identical row appears in the cross-objective filtering log in
`2_make_DART_results.Rmd`, where it can be read against the other objectives.

```{r results-5_summary, echo = F}
fl <- .st$filter_log
knitr::kable(
  fl,
  col.names = c('Objective', 'Cover', 'Min Pixels per Tx x Eco', '# Tx x Eco Excluded',
                '# Tx Depopulated', '# Eco Depopulated', 'Min Pixels per Year',
                'Year Truncated At', '# Years Dropped', '% Pixels Lost',
                '# Tx Absent', '# Eco Absent')
)
```

**Table.** One row for this objective x cover response. `% Pixels Lost` is the combined cost of all
three filters, not the cell filter alone. `# Tx Absent` / `# Eco Absent` count levels missing from
the post-filter data for any reason, which is a different quantity from the two depopulated columns:
a level that only ever appeared in sparse cells disappears without the depopulation filter being
involved.

Post-filter, this objective x cover response retains `r sum(tx_post_n)` pixels across
`r length(tx_post_n)` treatment level(s) and `r length(eco_post_n)` ecoregion level(s), the smallest
surviving totals being `r min(tx_post_n)` pixels for a treatment and `r min(eco_post_n)` for an
ecoregion, against a per-cell threshold of `r min_txeco_n_i`.

##### Interpretation

```{r results-5_interp, echo = F}
# Hand-written - edit the bullets here. Emitted immediately below, and collected
# into the consolidated section at the end of the document from this one place,
# so the two can never disagree.
interp_text[['increase_shr_SHR']] <- c(
  "- Mostly same considerations as `increase_pfg`",
  "- Time effects are negative immediately after treatment, then stay generally positive",
  "- Treatment looked generally successful."
)

# CLAUDE: model-generated bullets below, marked as such in the rendered text so
# their provenance is visible. Every number is computed from the objects this
# section already built, so none of it is typed in and none of it can drift from
# the tables above.
cl_b1  <- sig_by_bin[1, ]
cl_bn  <- sig_by_bin[nrow(sig_by_bin), ]
cl_ci  <- if (int_word == 'positive') 'mean_pct_sig_pos' else 'mean_pct_sig_neg'
cl_cu  <- if (int_word == 'positive') 'mean_pct_sig_neg' else 'mean_pct_sig_pos'
cl_pki <- peak_effect[peak_effect$direction == int_word, ]
cl_pku <- peak_effect[peak_effect$direction == uni_word, ]
cl_txb <- res_tx$summary[which.max(res_tx$summary$n_pix), ]
cl_ecot <- res_eco$summary[1, ]
cl_solo <- overlap_tbl$pct_pix[overlap_tbl$co_occurring_objective == 'none']
cl_co   <- overlap_tbl[overlap_tbl$co_occurring_objective != 'none', ][1, ]
cl_pb   <- res_tx$summary[res_tx$summary$tx_coarse == 'prescribed burn', ]

interp_text[['increase_shr_SHR']] <- c(
  interp_text[['increase_shr_SHR']],
  sprintf(
    "- CLAUDE: Call this the weakest of the four objectives that came out in the intended direction rather than a straightforward success: %.1f%% intended against %.1f%% unintended is only %.1f:1, so roughly a third of the significant pixels moved the wrong way.",
    int_effect$pct_sig_int, int_effect$pct_sig_und,
    int_effect$pct_sig_int / int_effect$pct_sig_und
  ),
  sprintf(
    "- CLAUDE: The knock-down-then-recover reading above is the best-supported timing statement in the report, because both sides of it rest on large samples: the unintended peak is at year %s (%.1f, n = %d significant pixels, the largest count behind any peak in the document) against an intended peak at year %s (%.1f, n = %d). The year bins agree - the unintended rate falls from %.2f%% to %.2f%% across the record while the intended rate falls more slowly, %.2f%% to %.2f%%.",
    cl_pku$peak_year, cl_pku$peak_effect, cl_pku$peak_n_pix,
    cl_pki$peak_year, cl_pki$peak_effect, cl_pki$peak_n_pix,
    cl_b1[[cl_cu]], cl_bn[[cl_cu]], cl_b1[[cl_ci]], cl_bn[[cl_ci]]
  ),
  sprintf(
    "- CLAUDE: This objective is not an independent sample in any meaningful sense - %.2f%% of its pixels carry no other objective and %.2f%% also carry `%s`. It is best reported as the shrub-response arm of the same treatments `increase_pfg` describes. It also shares %.2f%% of its pixels with `decrease_afg`, whose unintended positive result is the opposite reading of overlapping ground.",
    cl_solo, cl_co$pct_pix, cl_co$co_occurring_objective,
    overlap_tbl$pct_pix[overlap_tbl$co_occurring_objective == 'decrease_afg']
  ),
  sprintf(
    "- CLAUDE: The treatment ordering does *not* repeat the pattern seen for `increase_pfg` and `decrease_tre`, and that is worth stating as a difference rather than smoothing over. The top rate (`%s`, %.2f%%) sits on only %s pixels, and the two largest treatments diverge the wrong way: `%s` at %s pixels returns %.2f%% while `%s` at %s pixels returns %.2f%%. Adding soil disturbance to seeding does not help shrub recovery the way it helps perennial grass. `prescribed burn` is again near the bottom (%.2f%%, rank %d of %d).",
    res_tx$summary$tx_coarse[1], res_tx$summary$pct_sig[1],
    format(res_tx$summary$n_pix[1], big.mark = ','),
    cl_txb$tx_coarse, format(cl_txb$n_pix, big.mark = ','), cl_txb$pct_sig,
    res_tx$summary$tx_coarse[order(-res_tx$summary$n_pix)][2],
    format(sort(res_tx$summary$n_pix, decreasing = T)[2], big.mark = ','),
    res_tx$summary$pct_sig[order(-res_tx$summary$n_pix)][2],
    cl_pb$pct_sig, match('prescribed burn', res_tx$summary$tx_coarse), nrow(res_tx$summary)
  ),
  sprintf(
    "- CLAUDE: The top ecoregion here (`%s`, %.2f%% intended on %s pixels) is the same cell that tops `increase_pfg`, so one small high-elevation area drives the best result for both shrub and perennial-grass increase. Confirming it is a real effect rather than a sampling artefact needs either the environmental context or more pixels from that ecoregion.",
    cl_ecot$us_l4name, cl_ecot$pct_sig, format(cl_ecot$n_pix, big.mark = ',')
  )
)
```

`r paste(interp_text[['increase_shr_SHR']], collapse = '\n')`


---

## Overall results and interpretation, all objectives

The five objective x cover response sections above each end with their own summary statistics and
interpretation, written next to the evidence they describe. This section puts the same material side
by side, which is where one objective can be read against another. Nothing here is a second copy:
the filtering table is compiled from the same per-objective rows, and the interpretation text is
emitted from the same character vectors those sections define, so the two presentations cannot
disagree.

Two standing caveats apply to everything below. The objective groupings are **not a partition** - a
pixel counts toward an objective if it fell in any part of that objective, so multi-objective
treatments appear in several groupings and parts of the dataset are counted more than once. And an
objective/response pairing is only included when the response cover type matches the objective's
target cover, with bare ground the sole exception.

### Sample-size filtering across objectives

```{r overall_filter_log, echo = F}
# Compiled from the same per-objective rows each section reports, so this table
# and the one-row tables above cannot disagree. Thresholds differ by objective,
# which is exactly what this table exists to make visible: a compiled table
# built on unequal thresholds is comparing unequally filtered samples.
fl_all <- collect_obj_tables('filter_log_')

knitr::kable(
  fl_all,
  col.names = c('Objective', 'Cover', 'Min Pixels per Tx x Eco', '# Tx x Eco Excluded',
                '# Tx Depopulated', '# Eco Depopulated', 'Min Pixels per Year',
                'Year Truncated At', '# Years Dropped', '% Pixels Lost',
                '# Tx Absent', '# Eco Absent')
)
```

**Table.** One row per objective x cover response. `% Pixels Lost` is the combined cost of all three
filters. Read the `Min Pixels per Tx x Eco` column before comparing any two rows of any compiled
table in this project: where it differs, the rows describe differently filtered samples.

### Interpretation by objective

```{r overall_interp, echo = F}
# Emitted from the `interp_text` vectors defined in each objective's own section
# above - this chunk adds the headings and nothing else, so editing a bullet in
# one place changes both presentations of it.
interp_blocks <- unlist(lapply(names(interp_text), function(nm) {
  c(paste0('#### ', print_summary_name(summaries, match(nm, names(summaries)), 5)),
    '', interp_text[[nm]], '')
}))
```

`r paste(interp_blocks, collapse = '\n')`
